messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike detected for /v1/streaming (eu-west-1). p95=230ms -> 980ms, p99=640ms -> 2.3s. Error budget at risk. Auto-incident created: INC-2026-058
elaine_oncall: thanks, seeing it on my dashboard. I’m taking initial triage. tagging @kiran_prefetch and @nick_sre
nick_sre: I’m on it. first glance: large increase in backend fetches from KV store and a corresponding drop in prefix-cache hit rate. metrics here: https://obs.internal/graphs?panel=prefix_hitrate&e=now-1h to now
kiran_prefetch: yikes. I just rolled murmur-hash v2 to pref/cache last night (~01:10 UTC). Could be salt/hash change causing namespace split and low hit-rate. Current prefetch hitrate: 9% (was ~91% before deploy).
elaine_oncall: copy. Kiran, can you confirm which subset of shards got the new hash? list of recent deploys?
kiran_prefetch: checking.. `kubectl -n runtime get deploy prefetch-agent -o yaml | grep image` shows `prefetch-agent:murmur-v2` on cluster eu-west-1b only. Control plane flagged canary=10%.
ops_deploy: @kiran_prefetch we have canary traffic routed to subset; autoscaler seems fine. rollout was staged but something in prefix computation changed even for non-canary due to shared library bump in edge layer earlier today.
nick_sre: observable corollary: streaming stalls increase when prefix miss triggers synchronous KV fetch. tail path waits for store read and filesystem page-in. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T01:22:33Z ERR stream: prefix-miss fetcher latency=1120ms key=shard-47
2026-03-15T01:22:34Z WARN cache: prefetch miss bulk-fetch duration=2.4s keys=120
```
elaine_oncall: that aligns w/ p99 spike. For live mitigation: can we route traffic off the v2 canary or hotfix the prefactor?
kiran_prefetch: immediate mitigations: 1) revert murmur-v2 on prefetch-agent in eu-west-1b, 2) increase prefetch TTL to 60s and enable aggressive warming for top-100k prefix keys, 3) enable soft-stale responses for streaming until cache warms. Revert command: `kubectl -n runtime set image deployment/prefetch-agent prefetch-agent=prefetch-agent:murmur-v1 --record`
ops_deploy: rolling revert now to v1 on eu-west-1b canary pool. initiating: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/prefetch-agent -n runtime --to-revision=12`
observability-bot: [METRIC ALERT] prefix_cache_hitrate (eu-west-1) at 9% -> adapt. I will annotate timeline and keep 30s pulls.
maria_cs: Heads-up: Customer impact — we have 3 enterprise customers with heavy streaming usage in eu-west-1. One (AcmePay) reported degraded UX via support ticket #8732. I’ll prep the CS note after we assess mitigation ETA.
nick_sre: quick check: are we seeing cross-region fallback? Smart routing may send requests to other variants but some clients pin region via latency-based routing. We might need to failover traffic for high-SLA customers.
elaine_oncall: good point. Kiran, can we temporarily route enterprise customers to eu-central-1 for reads while cache warms?
kiran_prefetch: We can add a route rule for customer tag enterprise: `route-policy add --match customer_tag=enterprise --to region=eu-central-1` — needs config rollout (5s). But that would increase cross-region cost; acceptable for mitigation.
ops_deploy: doing route update for AcmePay and two others now. Patching edge config with canary=1.
elaine_oncall: monitoring p99 now. Nick, check streaming tail buffer sizes to avoid OOMs when many backend fetches queued.
nick_sre: increasing stream worker pool from 64 -> 96 for eu-west-1 to reduce queuing while revert completes. Patch applied.
observability-bot: [ANNOTATION] rollbacks and route patches at 01:28:12 UTC.
ops_deploy: revert completed on canary subset at 01:29:08 UTC. Hitrate improving but still low due to namespace split across many nodes; warming underway. current prefix hitrate: 28%
kiran_prefetch: warming job launched: `python tools/warm_prefixes.py --top 100k --concurrency 200` — expected warmup 6-8 minutes. Also enabling soft-stale: `config set streaming.soft_stale=true` for eu-west-1
maria_cs: drafting customer message: short summary + ETA 15–20min for visible improvements, ask to escalate if latency persists. I’ll hold send until p99 drops <800ms for 5m window.
elaine_oncall: agree. Nick, any residual errors?
nick_sre: error rates (5xx) remain nominal. This is latency-only; no 5xx surge. p99 trending: 2.3s -> 1.1s after revert and route patch.
elaine_oncall: good. We should capture postmortem seeds: root cause hypothesis = murmur-hash v2 changed bucketization so previously collocated prefixes are split -> prefetch inefficiency -> low hitrate -> backend fetch amplification -> streaming tail latency.
kiran_prefetch: adding to incident doc: `root_cause_candidates: hash_algo_change, library side-effect in edge, canary config leak`. Also note: prefetch warmup algorithm assumed stable namespace; we need to add a guard: if observed hitrate delta > 20% within 15min of deploy, auto-rollback.
ops_deploy: will open PR for deployguard and add canary isolation tests.
maria_cs: sending interim update to affected customers now: "We've identified a cache mismatch after a canary deploy that caused temporary increases in request latency. Our engineers reverted the canary and applied mitigations; visible improvement expected within 15 minutes. We can open a postmortem and will follow up"
elaine_oncall: thanks @maria_cs. On-call handoff plan: I’ll stay until p99<700ms for 20m. If stable, I’ll hand off to night oncall (nick_sre) with checklist: revert confirmed, warming done, route rules reverted, postmortem draft in INC-2026-058.
kiran_prefetch: warming complete at 01:36:50 UTC. final measured hitrate back to 86%.
nick_sre: p99 now 410ms, p95 120ms. Streaming stalls count down to baseline. Ready to take handoff if you want to step out, @elaine_oncall.
elaine_oncall: I’m stepping out. Handoff: observed root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps taken (revert, warming, route), customer notifications sent. Handoff note: priority = medium (SLO threatened but recovered); follow up items: deployment guard, canary isolation fix, add prefix-namespace regression test to CI. Tagging @kiran_prefetch for follow-ups.
ops_deploy: created ticket OPS-1294 for canary isolation + guard, assigned to kiran_prefetch.
elaine_oncall: thanks team. Closing live bridge. Please add any additional notes to INC-2026-058 doc and link postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
observability-bot: [RESOLVED] p99 alert resolved at 01:39:15 UTC. Incident auto-ack cleared.
maria_cs: adding final customer follow-up note and will coordinate SRE postmortem summary for execs.
kiran_prefetch: quick action items I’ll own: 1) revert-proof canary, 2) auto-rollback on hitrate delta, 3) add unit test for hashing consistency, 4) run canary replay next deploy. ETA for PRs: 48h.
nick_sre: will draft postmortem and include timeline + logs + mitigation commands used.
elaine_oncall: handed off to @nick_sre at 01:40:00 UTC. Closing thread.
